name: Williamstown
notes: Port Phillip Bay - sheltered from ocean swell by The Heads; expect local wind chop to dominate over model swell/wave figures

name: Robe
notes: SA Limestone Coast - open to Southern Ocean swell via Guichen Bay, partial shelter from the south/west

name: Port MacDonnell
notes: SA Limestone Coast, near the Victorian border - fully exposed Southern Ocean coastline

name: Cape Bridgewater
notes: West side of the Portland peninsula - fully exposed to Southern Ocean swell, generally the rougher side of Portland

name: Portland Bay
notes: East/harbour side of the Portland peninsula - more sheltered than Cape Bridgewater, faces Portland Bay

name: Bay of Islands
notes: Great Ocean Road, between Peterborough and Warrnambool - exposed Southern Ocean coastline, rugged limestone coast

name: Cape Otway Lightstation
notes: Southernmost tip of the Otway coast - fully exposed to Bass Strait/Southern Ocean, one of the most swell-exposed points on this list

name: Apollo Bay
notes: East side of Cape Otway - some shelter from the cape itself, still open to Bass Strait swell

name: Kennett River
notes: Great Ocean Road between Apollo Bay and Lorne - open Bass Strait coastline (note: corrected from 'Kennee River')

name: Torquay
notes: Surf Coast at the entrance to Port Phillip Bay/Bass Strait junction - open coast, popular surf/dive area

name: Port Phillip Heads (J5 Submarine)
notes: Just outside Port Phillip Heads near Barwon Heads, the 'Victorian Ships' Graveyard' - strong tidal currents through The Rip, exposed to Bass Strait swell

name: Queenscliff
notes: Inside Port Phillip Heads opposite Point Nepean - strong tidal currents near The Rip, more sheltered than the open coast

name: Blairgowrie Back Beach
notes: Mornington Peninsula ocean side (Bass Strait) - exposed, distinct from the sheltered bay-side front beach

name: Cape Schanck
notes: Tip of the Mornington Peninsula - fully exposed to Bass Strait/Southern Ocean swell

name: Cape Paterson
notes: South Gippsland coast - exposed Bass Strait swell, reef and surf breaks

name: Wilsons Prom (West - Norman Bay)
notes: Tidal River/Norman Bay, west side of the Prom - faces Bass Strait/Waratah Bay

name: Wilsons Prom (East - Sealers Cove)
notes: Sealers Cove, east side of the Prom - faces Bass Strait/Corner Inlet, remote

name: Mallacoota
notes: Far East Gippsland near the NSW border - exposed Bass Strait/Tasman Sea coast

name: Eden
notes: NSW far south coast - Twofold Bay gives some shelter, open Tasman Sea nearby

name: Green Cape
notes: Headland south of Eden in Beowa National Park - fully exposed Tasman Sea, strong currents

name: Tathra
notes: NSW far south coast - open Tasman Sea, small wharf area gives minor shelter

name: Bermagui
notes: NSW far south coast - open Tasman Sea, popular game-fishing/dive town

name: Narooma
notes: NSW far south coast - open Tasman Sea with a sheltered inlet/bar entrance nearby

name: Batemans Bay (Inside)
notes: Inside the Clyde River estuary/bay - sheltered from ocean swell

name: Batemans Bay (Outside)
notes: Ocean side near the bay entrance/heads - open Tasman Sea

name: Ulladulla
notes: NSW south coast - small harbour gives some shelter, open coast nearby (corrected from 'Uladulla')

name: Jervis Bay (Inside)
notes: Inside Jervis Bay near Huskisson - well sheltered, often calmer/clearer water

name: Jervis Bay (Outside - Point Perpendicular)
notes: At the bay entrance - fully exposed Tasman Sea, dramatic cliffs, strong currents

name: Shellharbour
notes: Illawarra coast - semi-sheltered small harbour, open coast nearby

name: Terrigal
notes: Central Coast NSW - open Tasman Sea, headland gives partial shelter

name: Fingal Bay
notes: Near Nelson Bay/Port Stephens - moderately sheltered bay next to Fingal Spit

name: Broughton Island
notes: Offshore island off Port Stephens - exposed, renowned dive location

name: Seal Rocks
notes: Mid-north coast NSW - open Tasman Sea, popular dive/surf spot

name: Forster
notes: Great Lakes region NSW - open ocean side, with sheltered lake systems nearby

name: South West Rocks
notes: Mid-north coast NSW near Trial Bay - Trial Bay gives some shelter, open coast nearby
